html:
The Guató are a canoe people of the Pantanal, the great seasonal wetland of the upper Paraguay River in western Brazil, in Mato Grosso and Mato Grosso do Sul. They lived on the water, spearing fish and caimans, gathering wild rice and moving with the floods, and camped on raised earth mounds called aterros.

Their language is usually placed in the Macro-Jê family. Ranchers took the Pantanal's dry ground in the 1800s, and the Paraguayan War brought armies into the region in the 1860s. By the mid 1900s officials declared the Guató extinct, but in the 1970s scattered families were found living in the towns, and in the 1990s they won back land on the island of Ínsua.
